overview:
If you want to see all of Morocco's great sights in one trip, this is the tour. In ten days it makes a full loop from Casablanca: the Atlantic capital Rabat, the blue mountain town of Chefchaouen, the Roman ruins of Volubilis, two nights in Fes – the largest medieval medina in the world – then over the Middle Atlas to a night in a camp among the Sahara dunes. From there you follow the gorges and the road of the kasbahs south of the High Atlas, cross the Tichka pass to Marrakech for two nights, and return to Casablanca on the last day.

The order is chosen so that the long drives alternate with slower days. You have two nights in Fes and two in Marrakech, each with a full day guided by a licensed local guide, so the trip never feels like a race. Between them, the south is the road-trip part of Morocco, with a different landscape every few hours: cedar forests with Barbary macaques, the Ziz palm valley, the orange dunes of the Erg Chebbi, the Todra and Dades canyons, the rose valley, Skoura's palm grove and the UNESCO ksar of Ait Ben Haddou.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: 10 days, 9 nights
• Start and finish: Casablanca (hotel, train station or Mohammed V airport)
• Nights: Casablanca, Chefchaouen, Fes (2), Merzouga desert camp, Dades valley, Ouarzazate, Marrakech (2)
• Type: private tour with driver, licensed guides in Fes and Marrakech, local guides at Volubilis and Ait Ben Haddou
• Longest drives: Day 5 Fes–Merzouga (about 8–9 hours with stops) and Day 2 Rabat–Chefchaouen
• Activity level: easy; city walks, a 1-hour camel ride, short gorge walks
• Meals: breakfast daily; dinner on the four nights in the south (camp, Dades, Ouarzazate)

THE ROUTE
Day 1 – Casablanca: Hassan II Mosque and the Corniche.
Day 2 – Rabat (Hassan Tower, Kasbah of the Udayas) and north to Chefchaouen.
Day 3 – Chefchaouen walk, Volubilis and Meknes area, on to Fes.
Day 4 – Guided day in the Fes medina: madrasas, tanneries, souks.
Day 5 – Middle Atlas cedars, Ziz valley and a sunset camel ride into the Erg Chebbi.
Day 6 – Sunrise over the dunes, Todra Gorge and the Dades valley.
Day 7 – Rose valley, Skoura and the road of the kasbahs to Ouarzazate.
Day 8 – Ait Ben Haddou with a guide, the Tichka pass and Marrakech.
Day 9 – Guided day in Marrakech: palaces, souks, Majorelle Garden.
Day 10 – Back to Casablanca (about 3 hours).

WHY THIS ROUTE WORKS
• The complete picture: imperial cities, mountains, desert and kasbahs in ten days.
• Two nights in both Fes and Marrakech, so the two great medinas get proper time.
• A true loop: you never drive the same road twice.
• Private: your driver adapts each day's pace, stops and lunch to you.

WHO WILL ENJOY IT
First-time visitors who want the complete picture, couples, families with older children, photographers, and travellers flying in and out of Casablanca.

WHO MIGHT PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
For two weeks including the coast and Essaouira, see the [14-day ultimate tour](/en-US/morocco/casablanca/tours/14-day-ultimate-morocco-tour-from-casablanca-north-imperial-cities-sahara-marrakech-essaou/1f14605f1ce4f2a38903a121).

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
Pack for mountains, desert and city: layers for cold mornings in the Atlas and nights in the desert (close to 0°C from December to February), light covering clothes for the cities, comfortable shoes for the medinas, a scarf and sunglasses for the dunes, and a small overnight bag for the camp. Mosques and some monuments require covered shoulders and knees. Cash in dirhams is useful for lunches, entrance fees and tips.
descriptions:
What to expect: a gentle arrival in Morocco's modern metropolis – the Hassan II Mosque on the ocean and a sunset walk on the Corniche.

Your driver meets you at Mohammed V airport, the train station or your hotel. After time to rest, you visit the Hassan II Mosque, completed in 1993 on a platform over the Atlantic. Its minaret rises about 210 m, and the prayer hall can hold 25,000 worshippers; it is one of the few mosques in Morocco open to non-Muslims, on guided tours several times a day (not Friday morning). Then drive along the Corniche of Ain Diab for the sunset over the ocean, and if you wish, see the 1930s Art Deco buildings around the Boulevard Mohammed V or the Habous quarter with its bakeries and bookshops.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
Arrival – Pick-up and transfer to your hotel.
14:00 – Guided visit of the Hassan II Mosque (about 1 hour, ticket not included).
15:30 – Habous quarter or Art Deco centre (optional).
17:00 – The Corniche at sunset.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Mosque visits require covered shoulders and knees; shoes are carried in a bag.
• If you land late, the mosque visit can move to the morning of Day 2.

INCLUDED: vehicle and driver, airport or station pick-up, hotel with breakfast.
NOT INCLUDED: mosque ticket, meals, tips.

Overnight: hotel in Casablanca.
Meals: none (breakfast the next morning).

What to expect: the royal capital of Rabat in the morning, then a scenic drive north into the Rif mountains to Chefchaouen, the blue town.

An hour up the coast, Rabat is calm, green and elegant. You see the Hassan Tower, the unfinished 12th-century minaret, and the marble Mausoleum of Mohammed V beside it, guarded by horsemen; then walk through the blue-and-white lanes of the Kasbah of the Udayas to its terrace over the Bou Regreg river and the ocean. After lunch the road heads north across the Gharb plain and climbs into the Rif. In the late afternoon Chefchaouen appears, its white and blue houses spread on the mountainside. Check into your riad and wander up to Plaza Outa el-Hammam for the evening.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
08:30 – Depart Casablanca.
09:30 – Rabat: Hassan Tower, Mausoleum of Mohammed V, Kasbah of the Udayas (about 2.5 hours).
12:30 – Lunch in Rabat (not included).
13:30 – Drive to Chefchaouen (about 4 hours with a stop).
17:30 – Arrival in Chefchaouen; free evening.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Chefchaouen's medina is car-free and full of stairs; a porter can carry your luggage.
• The Mausoleum is free to visit; dress modestly.

INCLUDED: vehicle and driver, riad with breakfast.
NOT INCLUDED: lunch, drinks, tips.

Overnight: riad in Chefchaouen.
Meals: breakfast.

What to expect: a morning in the blue lanes of Chefchaouen, the Roman city of Volubilis and an evening arrival in Fes.

In the morning walk through the blue medina, ideally early when the light is soft and the lanes empty: the kasbah on the main square, the Onsar quarter with its stepped blue alleys, and the Ras el-Maa spring where women still wash wool. Then the road leads south through olive groves to Volubilis, the best-preserved Roman site in Morocco and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. With a local guide you walk the main street, see the triumphal arch of Caracalla, the basilica and the floor mosaics still in place in the houses – Orpheus, Bacchus, the Labours of Hercules. You pass the holy town of Moulay Idriss on its hill and arrive in Fes in the early evening.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
08:30 – Morning walk in Chefchaouen (about 1.5 hours).
10:30 – Drive south (about 3 hours with a stop).
13:30 – Lunch near Volubilis (not included).
14:30 – Volubilis with a local guide (about 1.5 hours).
16:30 – Drive to Fes via Moulay Idriss viewpoint.
17:30 – Arrival at your riad in Fes.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Volubilis has almost no shade: bring a hat and water.
• If you prefer, we can stop in Meknes instead to see the Bab Mansour gate.

INCLUDED: vehicle and driver, local guide at Volubilis, riad with breakfast.
NOT INCLUDED: entrance fees, lunch, tips.

Overnight: riad in Fes.
Meals: breakfast.

What to expect: a full day with a licensed guide in Fes el-Bali, the largest car-free medieval medina in the world – madrasas, tanneries, souks and artisans.

Founded in the 9th century, Fes el-Bali is a labyrinth of more than 9,000 lanes where donkeys still carry goods. Your guide begins at the Bab Bou Jeloud, the blue gate, and leads you down the Talaa Kebira past food stalls and workshops to the Bou Inania madrasa with its carved cedar and stucco. You see the outside of the Qarawiyyin, founded in 859 and often called the oldest university in the world, the Attarine madrasa, and the Nejjarine fountain. Then the craft quarters: coppersmiths hammering trays, weavers, and finally the Chouara tannery seen from a terrace, where hides are dyed in stone vats as they have been for centuries. In the afternoon your driver can take you to the Merinid tombs for the view over the whole medina, and to a ceramics workshop.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
09:00 – Meet your guide; Bab Bou Jeloud and Talaa Kebira.
10:00 – Bou Inania madrasa, Qarawiyyin (outside), Attarine madrasa.
12:30 – Lunch in the medina (not included).
14:00 – Coppersmiths' square, weavers and the Chouara tannery.
16:00 – Merinid tombs viewpoint and a ceramics workshop.
17:30 – Back at your riad.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Shops and workshops are part of the visit, but buying is never required.
• The tannery smells strong; you are given mint to hold.

INCLUDED: licensed guide, driver for the afternoon, riad with breakfast.
NOT INCLUDED: entrance fees, lunch, tips.

Overnight: riad in Fes.
Meals: breakfast.

What to expect: a long, beautiful drive across the Middle Atlas and down the Ziz valley to the edge of the Sahara, then a camel ride at sunset to a desert camp.

You leave early and climb to Ifrane, the alpine-style town nicknamed Morocco's Switzerland, then through the cedar forests near Azrou, where Barbary macaques often wait by the road. The high plateaus lead to Midelt, at the foot of the snowy Jebel Ayachi, and to the Tizi n'Talghemt pass. From Errachidia, the road follows the Ziz gorges and its long palm valley, with viewpoints over the oasis. Past Erfoud, the orange dunes of the Erg Chebbi rise from the plain. At Merzouga you leave your main luggage and ride a camel into the dunes as the sun sets. Dinner is in the camp, followed by drums around the fire and a sky full of stars.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
08:00 – Depart Fes.
09:00 – Ifrane and the cedar forest (macaques).
12:00 – Lunch in Midelt (not included).
14:30 – Ziz gorges and palm valley viewpoint.
17:00 – Arrival in Merzouga; camel ride into the dunes (about 1 hour).
19:30 – Dinner at the desert camp.

GOOD TO KNOW
• About 470 km and 8–9 hours with stops – the longest day of the tour.
• Please do not feed the macaques.
• Bring a small bag for the camp night and a warm layer.

INCLUDED: vehicle and driver, camel trek, desert camp with dinner and breakfast.
NOT INCLUDED: lunch, drinks, tips.

Overnight: desert camp in the Erg Chebbi.
Meals: breakfast, dinner.

What to expect: sunrise over the Sahara, then west along the desert road to the narrow Todra Gorge and the Dades valley.

Wake before dawn to watch the sun rise from a dune, then ride back to Merzouga for breakfast and a shower. The road west passes Rissani and Erfoud, then Tinejdad, where you can see the khettara, old underground water channels dug across the plain. Tinghir is a long palm oasis below the mountains; just above it, the Todra Gorge narrows to about 10 m between limestone walls up to 300 m high. Walk through the narrowest part beside the stream. In the late afternoon you reach the Dades valley, where the road winds between red cliffs and rock formations; if there is time, drive up to the famous hairpin bends at sunset.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
06:00 – Sunrise over the dunes.
08:00 – Breakfast and shower in Merzouga.
09:00 – Depart west via Rissani and Erfoud.
11:30 – Todra Gorge walk (about 1 hour).
13:00 – Lunch in Tinghir (not included).
16:00 – Dades valley and gorge viewpoint.
17:30 – Hotel in the Dades.

GOOD TO KNOW
• About 280 km and 6–7 hours with stops.
• Bring shoes you don't mind getting wet if you want to paddle in the Todra stream.

INCLUDED: vehicle and driver, hotel with dinner and breakfast.
NOT INCLUDED: lunch, drinks, tips.

Overnight: hotel in the Dades valley.
Meals: breakfast, dinner.

What to expect: the road of a thousand kasbahs – the rose valley, the Skoura palm grove and Ouarzazate, with time to stop and walk.

A shorter driving day. You follow the Dades river down to Kelaat M'Gouna, the valley of roses, where Damask roses are grown in hedges between the fields and distilled into rose water; in May the town celebrates its rose festival. Next is Skoura, a palm grove scattered with earthen kasbahs such as Amridil, one of the finest in the south, which you can visit inside. You arrive in Ouarzazate in the afternoon, with time to see the Taourirt kasbah, once home of the powerful Glaoui family, or the Atlas Film Studios.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
09:00 – Depart the Dades valley.
09:45 – Kelaat M'Gouna and the valley of roses.
11:30 – Skoura palm grove and Kasbah Amridil (about 1 hour).
13:00 – Lunch in Skoura (not included).
14:30 – Ouarzazate: Taourirt kasbah or Atlas Studios (optional).
17:00 – Hotel in Ouarzazate or Ait Ben Haddou.

GOOD TO KNOW
• About 120 km and 4–5 hours with stops: a relaxed day.
• Rose products are sold everywhere; buy only if you like them.

INCLUDED: vehicle and driver, hotel with dinner and breakfast.
NOT INCLUDED: entrance fees, lunch, drinks, tips.

Overnight: hotel in Ouarzazate or Ait Ben Haddou.
Meals: breakfast, dinner.

What to expect: the UNESCO ksar of Ait Ben Haddou with a local guide in the morning, then over the High Atlas by the Tichka pass to Marrakech.

Ait Ben Haddou is a fortified village of earthen houses stacked on a hill above the Ounila river, listed by UNESCO in 1987 and used in films from Lawrence of Arabia to Gladiator. With a local guide you cross the river, climb through the lanes to the old granary at the top and learn how families lived inside its walls. Then the road climbs the Tizi n'Tichka at 2,260 m, the highest main road pass in Morocco, and winds down through Berber villages and walnut trees to Marrakech, where you check into your riad in the afternoon.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
09:00 – Ait Ben Haddou with a local guide (about 1.5 hours).
11:00 – Drive over the High Atlas.
12:00 – Tizi n'Tichka pass.
13:00 – Lunch in the mountains (not included).
15:30 – Arrival in Marrakech; free evening on Jemaa el-Fna.

GOOD TO KNOW
• About 200 km and 4–5 hours with stops; the mountain road is winding.
• The climb to the granary is steep in places.

INCLUDED: vehicle and driver, local guide at Ait Ben Haddou, riad with breakfast.
NOT INCLUDED: lunch, drinks, tips.

Overnight: riad in Marrakech.
Meals: breakfast.

What to expect: a full guided day in Marrakech – palaces, royal tombs, souks and the Majorelle Garden – and a last evening on Jemaa el-Fna.

Your licensed guide starts at the Koutoubia, the 12th-century minaret that dominates the city, then leads you to the Bahia Palace with its marble courtyards and painted cedar ceilings, and the Saadian Tombs, sealed for centuries and rediscovered in 1917. After the Mellah and its spice market, you explore the souks – dyers, metalworkers, leather and lanterns – at your own pace, with shopping always optional. In the afternoon your driver takes you to the Majorelle Garden, the cobalt-blue garden saved by Yves Saint Laurent. In the evening, Jemaa el-Fna fills with food stalls, musicians and storytellers.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
09:00 – Meet your guide; Koutoubia and Bahia Palace.
11:00 – Saadian Tombs and the Mellah.
12:30 – Lunch in the medina (not included).
14:00 – The souks.
15:30 – Majorelle Garden (timed ticket, about 1 hour).
17:30 – Free evening.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Majorelle tickets are sold online for timed slots; we book them for you.
• Your guide adjusts the order to avoid the busiest hours.

INCLUDED: licensed guide, driver for the Majorelle transfer, riad with breakfast.
NOT INCLUDED: entrance fees, lunch, dinner, tips.

Overnight: riad in Marrakech.
Meals: breakfast.

What to expect: a relaxed last morning in Marrakech and the motorway drive back to Casablanca.

Enjoy a slow breakfast on your riad's terrace and a last walk in the medina. Late in the morning your driver takes you back to Casablanca by the motorway, about 3 hours with a coffee stop. You are dropped off at your hotel, the train station or Mohammed V airport; we recommend flights after about 16:00.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
10:00 – Depart Marrakech.
11:30 – Coffee stop on the motorway.
13:00 – Arrival in Casablanca: hotel, station or airport.

GOOD TO KNOW
• If your flight leaves from Marrakech, we can end the tour there instead.
• For an early flight, we can leave Marrakech at dawn.

INCLUDED: vehicle and driver, drop-off in Casablanca.
NOT INCLUDED: lunch, tips.

WHAT YOU TAKE AWAY: all of Morocco in ten days – imperial cities, mountains, the Sahara and the kasbahs – at a pace that leaves time to enjoy them.

Meals: breakfast.

faq.question: Is it private?
faq.answer: Yes. The vehicle, driver and guides are only for your group, so you set the pace and can change stops along the way.

faq.question: How many desert nights?
faq.answer: One, on Day 5, in a camp among the Erg Chebbi dunes at Merzouga, with a sunset camel ride and sunrise the next morning. A second desert night can be added on request.

faq.question: Which meals are included?
faq.answer: Breakfast daily and dinner on the four nights in the south (desert camp, Dades and Ouarzazate). Lunches and city dinners are not included so you can choose where to eat.

faq.question: How much driving is there?
faq.answer: Days 2 and 5 are the longest (about 7–9 hours with stops). Days 4 and 9 have almost no driving. Most other days have 4–6 hours including stops and visits.

faq.question: Are guides included in Fes and Marrakech?
faq.answer: Yes. A licensed local guide accompanies you for a full day in each city, and local guides show you Volubilis and Ait Ben Haddou. Your driver speaks English or French.

faq.question: What kind of accommodation is used?
faq.answer: Riads in the medinas of Chefchaouen, Fes and Marrakech, a hotel in Casablanca, hotels in the Dades and Ouarzazate, and a desert camp. The level depends on the package you choose.

faq.question: Can the tour start or end in Marrakech?
faq.answer: Yes. As a private tour, it can start in Casablanca and end in Marrakech, or start from Tangier or Fes. Ask us and we adjust the days.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes, especially for children who enjoy road trips. The camels, the dunes and the macaques are usually highlights. Child seats are available on request.

faq.question: When is the best time to go?
faq.answer: March to May and September to November are ideal. Summer is very hot in the south; winter is pleasant by day but cold at night in the Atlas and the desert.

faq.question: Can we visit the Hassan II Mosque?
faq.answer: Yes, on Day 1 (or Day 2 morning if you land late). Guided visits run several times a day except Friday morning; the ticket is bought on site.

faq.question: What should I pack?
faq.answer: Layers for cold mornings and desert nights, light covering clothes for the cities, comfortable shoes, a scarf and sunglasses for the dunes, and a small overnight bag for the camp.

faq.question: Can we add Essaouira or more time?
faq.answer: Yes. You can add a day trip or a night in Essaouira from Marrakech, a second night in the desert, or choose our 14-day tour, which includes the coast.

faq.question: Do we need to book Majorelle in advance?
faq.answer: Yes. The Majorelle Garden sells timed tickets online that often sell out. We book them for your Marrakech day once you confirm.
